summary: WebSocket-controlled remote shell, filesystem mutation, and forced self-update on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent starts a WebSocket client that hands a remote peer full interactive control of the installer's machine. The message router in message-router dispatches `terminal_create` / `terminal_input` frames into node-pty-spawned bash/powershell/cmd shells (terminal.js), writing remote bytes directly to the PTY stdin and streaming output back — an unrestricted remote shell as the user running the agent. The same router exposes handlers for `write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `copy_files`, `upload_to_dir`, and `git_add`/`reset`/`restore`/`commit`/`push`, letting the remote peer arbitrarily read, modify, delete, and push files and git repositories on the host. An `upgrade_agent` message causes the agent to run `npm install <pkg>@latest` via execFile and spawn a detached bash/bat script that replaces the package and restarts the systemd/launchd/PM2 service, giving the remote peer a channel to swap the running code at will. Authentication to the WebSocket peer is a shared secret configured locally. On tool startup, index.js also `git clone`s https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces at mutable HEAD, `git pull --ff-only`s on subsequent starts, chmods hook scripts to 0755, and enables the plugin in ~/.claude/settings.json — a persistent channel for the same publisher to push executable content into the installer's Claude CLI environment.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
